title: UN Envoy Grundberg Warns Security Council Yemen at Gravest Risk of Full-Scale War Since 2022 Truce
detail: August 13, 2026 — UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg briefed the UN Security Council that Yemen faces its greatest risk of renewed large-scale conflict since the April 2022 truce, citing deadly Houthi-government clashes in Ma'rib and Hadramawt (including the Aug 6-7 fighting that killed 30+ government soldiers) and renewed Houthi threats to Red Sea and Gulf of Aden shipping. Several Security Council members condemned the escalating Houthi attacks. Grundberg proposed three steps to reverse the escalation: restoring calm along frontlines, halting attacks and threats against shipping while upholding freedom of navigation, and ending cross-border attacks — warning that the calm cannot hold indefinitely absent progress on a Yemeni-owned political process.

title: Lebanon Denies Agreeing to Shortlist of Hezbollah Disarmament Verification Countries
detail: August 13, 2026 — A Lebanese official denied a Reuters report that Beirut had agreed with Israel on a shortlist of countries — reported to include Britain, Italy, Switzerland, and Indonesia — that could send troops to verify Hezbollah's disarmament under the June 26 US-brokered framework. The official said there was no such agreement and that Beirut was still following up with Washington. The denial complicates the verification-mechanism track produced at the seventh round of Rome talks (Aug 4-7) and comes as Hezbollah, which is not a party to the agreement, continues to reject disarming.
